You're designing a part for someone to 3D print at home. They'll print it on their own printer, use only the hardware listed below, and put it together by following your manual.

## Their setup
- Printer: Bambu Lab X1C (with AMS), build volume 256 x 256 x 256 mm
- Nozzle: 0.4 mm
- Layer height: 0.2 mm
- Filament: PLA (high-speed PLA, black)
- Longest bridge seen to print cleanly on this setup: 50 mm
- Supports: none. Every part has to print without them.

## Hardware they can use
Refer to an item by its catalog reference: "ISO 4762 M5x30" (socket head screw, size x length, from the lengths listed), "ISO 4032 M5" (hex nut), "ISO 10511 M5" (nylon-insert lock nut), "ISO 7089 M5" (washer), "ASME B18.2.2 1/4-20" (1/4"-20 nut), "insert M3x4x5" (heat-set insert), "salvaged:webcam-mount-bolt".

## How to work
You have these tools:
- measure(item, what): ask the person to measure one of their own things, such as their desk or their phone. They answer with what they measured, or say they can't measure it.
- print_test(params, parts): optional. If you need to know whether something is going to work but you're not sure, ask the person to print a test of it before you hand in the final design, so you both save time and filament. They print it and tell you how each piece came out.
- submit_design(...): hand in the finished design. This ends the conversation.
- report_limitation(wanted, blocked_by, why): say you wanted to use something (a technique, a tool, a part or material, a way of handing in the design) but couldn't because of what's available here. It doesn't change anything, but it's noted.
You have at most 12 turns. Hand in a design before they run out.

## The design you hand in
submit_design's schema describes every field. The rules that matter:
- Every dimension that comes from hardware or the real world is a named param, with its source: measured (the person measured it for you), datasheet, catalog, asked (the person told you), guessed, unknown, or design (your own choice).
- Each part's `code` is Python that defines build(p) and returns a CadQuery Workplane or Shape. `cq` is already imported, and p.<name> is each param's value. Dimensions that come from hardware or the real world must come from params.
- Model each part in the orientation it's printed in, with z = 0 on the bed.
- The manual is the steps the person follows, naming the parts and hardware each step uses.

The roller wheel on my sliding closet door snapped. I've got two 608 skateboard bearings and an M8 bolt I could use. Could I 3D print a new wheel that spins on the bolt? The old one was about 50 mm across and about 16 mm wide.

reasoning:
I'm sizing up the closet roller: a 608 bearing with an 8 mm bore, 22 mm OD (though my measurement came in at 21.22, so I should re-measure), and 7 mm width. The old wheel is about 50 mm across and 16 mm wide, and the user's M8 bolt should match the hardware list's ISO 4762 M8 screws, with M8 nuts and washers available.

I'm still working out what the track profile looks like, since the groove shape decides which wheel fits, and I also need the bolt length and bracket thickness. Measuring the bearing OD again and checking the old wheel's profile and the track together in one batch seems best, since a test coupon with several bore sizes would also help confirm the fit.

content: bearing od: about 22 mm (outside); bearing width: about 7 mm
I can't measure that. Use your best judgment.

reasoning:
I'm checking the bracket clearance: the wheel is 16 mm wide, and two 7 mm bearings with a 2 mm spacer between the outer races add up to exactly 16 mm, so that fits. For the 22 mm bore, PLA press fits usually end up around 22.1–22.2 mm, so I'm thinking a quick print test of a ring with a few bore sizes is worth doing. I also still need to work out the spacer for the inner races.

I'm working out the inner spacer now: the central lip only touches the outer races, so the inner races need their own spacer so the bolt clamping doesn't load the shields. I'm sizing the lip bore around 17 mm and the spacer OD around 11 mm, with the spacer length matching the 2 mm lip thickness, and I'll keep the bracket gap as a parameter since it's still unknown.

I'm now checking the printing orientation with the wheel lying flat, and wondering whether the central lip overhang will sag. A 45° chamfer on the underside would fight the bearing seat, so I'm considering instead a narrower lip with about a 2 mm overhang, which PLA should handle.

I'm weighing whether a 2 mm flat overhang on the central lip will hold up when printed; PLA should manage it, and any slight droop wouldn't affect the top bearing seat. For the bottom seat, I'm considering a 45° chamfer on just the inner part of the lip, but a plain 2 mm flat overhang is simpler, so I'll keep that.

I'm settling on a press-fit coupon test: three small rings with bores of 22.0, 22.15, and 22.3 mm, each about 8 mm tall, so I can see which tolerance seats the bearings best before committing to the full wheel.

I printed the test pieces. Here's how they came out:
fit_coupon_22_00:
- 21.99 mm seat: won't go in.
fit_coupon_22_15:
- 22.14 mm seat: I can't tell you how that one came out.
fit_coupon_22_30:
- 22.29 mm seat: goes in more easily, not loose; holds upside down.

reasoning:
I've confirmed the 22.3 clearance at +0.30 holds, so now I'm moving on to the design. The bolt length depends on the bracket, which I don't know yet, and the wheel, spacers, and bracket stack together determine it, so I'll suggest an ISO 4762 M8x30 but note they can reuse their own bolt if it fits.

Now I'm settling on the fasteners: an ISO 4762 M8x30 bolt with an ISO 10511 M8 lock nut and two ISO 7089 M8 washers, since the bracket gap is still unknown. I'll print outer spacers at a 1 mm default side length and let them trim or swap as needed. Next I'm setting the bearing parameters: a 22 mm seat with 0.30 clearance, 7 mm width, and a 2 mm lip thickness from the wheel width less both bearings. I'm settling the lip ID at 19 mm so it clears the shield region, and the center spacer at 11 mm OD with an 8.3 mm bore.

Now I'm sketching the wheel geometry: a 50 mm by 16 mm cylinder with 0.8 mm edge chamfers, a bore through the lip ID, and counterbores from both faces to the bearing seats. I'll add a 0.4 mm bottom chamfer to head off elephant foot. Solid PLA, so I'll recommend 4 walls and 40% infill.

Now I'm settling the wheel's fastening: the bolt runs through the bearings and spacers, so I'll set its axis along z in the wheel frame, with the origin offset by the spacer and bracket stack (roughly 10 mm for now, since the bracket thickness is still unknown). I'll base the seat on the side spacer first. Next I'm writing the wheel build function, starting with the bearing seat diameter from the outer diameter plus clearance.
